title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 16 | Week 6 vs. Los Angeles Rams
headline: Jeremiyah Love is out Sunday vs. the Rams with no IR talk; Bam Knight is the likely beneficiary, though LaFleur stopped short of confirming a role.
summary: LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love will miss this week's game, with no IR discussion and a reassessment planned for Monday. He called Love's cutting ability a strength but said his left foot is not right yet, and that playing him now would not be in his best interest. LaFleur spoke highly of Bam Knight, citing his strong performances when given chances, including in 2022 with LaFleur in New York, and said he will get his opportunity. Asked whether Tyler Allgeier would take the lion's share with Love out, LaFleur only said "we'll see." He said Josh Sweat is in a good spot and looks ready to compete, and that the Rams' tackle situation has Sweat's matchup in focus. He reported that a returning defensive back has had a great week of practice and feels good, and that another defensive back is still out one more week. On the broader outlook, he acknowledged the team's losing results over four weeks but emphasized competing and execution. Receivers Jalen and Reggie learned last week they would get increased roles, and LaFleur framed it as preparation for whatever happens during the week.

title: Joe Brady Talks Defense And Playing On A Short Week
headline: Ed Oliver, DJ Moore, Josh Palmer and Dee Alford are all listed questionable for the Raiders game, with Ed and DJ returning to full-speed work this week.
summary: Brady said Ed Oliver, DJ Moore, Josh Palmer and Dee Alford will all be questionable for the upcoming game. Oliver and Moore have been doing walkthroughs on the side, and Brady was glad to see them move around in practice. He will review how they feel after practice and on tape, and said that if they are ready to go, they will play. On defense, Brady wants players to trust one another and communicate rather than press and play outside the system, and he called the intensity and urgency in camp what he has been looking for. He stressed that walkthroughs are a key part of a short week because they are used to check technique, alignment, and knowledge of the game plan. Brady said the team is being set up well by the hotel and facility arrangements at UC Irvine, which he credited to Mr. Pegula. On Spencer, Brady said he is a tough player who has progressed back onto the practice field after leaving a game, and that he expects him to be ready. He said the kicker is in a great headspace after a big kick last week and that the team is making do without goalposts. On Josh Allen, Brady said the offense should stick to the system and take underneath throws when they are available, because that opens up the deep game, and that he wants Allen to keep his own style while focusing on ball security and staying on the field.

title: “It’s a Business Trip” | DeMeco Ryans Ahead of Texans vs. Jaguars
headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. to get 'as much action as he can handle' Sunday, Jaylin Noel's role is growing, and Jawhar Jordan steps up for David Montgomery vs. Jacksonville.
summary: Ryans said the Texans handled travel problems well: a plane change in Houston delayed the trip, but the team adjusted its schedule and the players responded. Practice in London was clean and focused on special situations, and most players slept on the flight, with the message now being to rest tonight. He called Jaylin Noel's rise a confidence-driven result of getting him the ball and big-play chances, and said Noel is also a punt and kick returner who can make impact plays. On receivers, Ryans said Marvin Harrison Jr. fits in without changing the offense, that the group welcomed him, and that the Texans will get him as much action as he can handle Sunday. He said the running game is in good hands with Jawhar Jordan stepping up this week for David Montgomery and with Woody Marks, and that the passing game has capable players if needed. Henry To'oTo'o had a good week of practice coming back from injury and is expected to play. Ryans said the Jaguars' extra days in London don't matter once the ball is kicked off, and that the team is excited about the historic stadium and London fans.

title: Coen on Readiness for Texans, Mental Toughness & Containing QB C.J. Stroud | Press Conference
headline: Coen stressed cutting self-inflicted penalties and staying on schedule against Houston; no clear player-specific fantasy signals came out of the presser.
summary: Coen praised the team's mental toughness after a close win over Philadelphia, saying most NFL games come down to one score. He said the pass rush has been affecting the quarterback in many ways, and that it will be needed against C.J. Stroud so Houston can't sit back and pick the defense apart. He hopes the secondary won't press for a first interception against Stroud, and wants more disciplined eyes in man coverage. On the long snapper, Coen said he won't get much work in practice today and the decision will come closer to game time. He explained why staying on schedule matters, warning that second-and-8 or longer pushes pressure onto the line and quarterback. He described how he adjusted play-calling late in the Philadelphia game, after a drive stalled past midfield, using a quick idea from a player that led to a key third-down conversion. He called the London week normal and said the team has spent more time together organically. He said facing a division rival means changing presentation through personnel, motions and disguises while keeping what has worked before. Finally, he said reducing penalties, which were around 12 or 13 last week, is a huge focus, with better hand placement on perimeter blocks.

topics.detail: Coen said roughly 12-13 penalties last week are a major focus this week, with better hand placement on perimeter blocks as a key fix.
Coen explained the importance of staying on schedule (second-and-8 or less), saying second-and-10 is manageable but longer distances are a problem, especially against Houston.

Coen said Houston's defensive line is strong and that the defense must limit C.J. Stroud's time in the pocket. Stroud has no interceptions, and Coen hopes the secondary won't press to get the first one.

Coen said the long snapper, referred to as Ross in the transcript, won't get much practice work today and will be evaluated closer to game time. Ross is not on the listed roster, so no injury entry was made.
Coen said division games call for adjustments in personnel, motions, shifts and defensive disguises while keeping tendencies that have worked before.
Coen said he likes being in London, the team is enjoying the change of scenery, and he expects a strong crowd at Sunday's game.
Coen said players have spent more time together informally this week, which he sees as a positive.

title: Klint Kubiak rules Tonka Hemingway out, previews Bills matchup
headline: Tonka Hemingway is out for Week 6 vs. Buffalo, and Jalen Nailor is back and available after missing last week; Trey Zuhn is questionable.
summary: Kubiak opened by ruling defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway out for this week and said Thornton and Runyan will not be elevated. He listed Trey Zuhn as questionable. Jalen Nailor will be available, and Kubiak praised his spacing and impact even though his catch numbers have not yet shown it, saying he is excited to have him back. He said Nailor's time off gave him a chance to freshen up and that he will be an impactful player this year. Kubiak said the team has responded well to a week of intentional coaching and described the group as mature and eager to win. He said the guard and cornerback competitions are pushing each player to improve, and that he knows who will play but is keeping it from the players. He called it very important for receivers to contribute more so defenses cannot focus on Brock Bowers, and said the staff has been working on that. On the defensive line, Kubiak said Hemingway has been a steady leader and the team will miss him, but his reps will go to other players.

title: Kellen Moore on injury report, Giants defense | Saints vs. Giants 2026 NFL Week 6
headline: Chris Olave (illness, limited) and Alvin Kamara (back, questionable) are the key fantasy watches; Kaden Elliss (calf) has no timeline.
summary: Moore opened with the injury report: two players are out with a calf issue, and Chris Olave and Nathan Shepherd are both limited by an illness. Alvin Kamara is questionable with a back issue. Moore said Olave has been sick for a few days, so returning to football takes time, but he did some good things at practice. On Kaden Elliss, Moore said the calf injury began after the Vegas game and has needed week-to-week management, and that he will return when ready. Moore described the illness as a general umbrella covering several classifications. He said the team has spoken with Mrs. B and that the team is focused on winning, calling it a good week of practice. On the Giants, Moore highlighted their turnover creation, physicality, and their competitiveness in close games. He also said the team is still finalizing plans for a potential trip to Paris.

title: Coach John Harbaugh provides final updates before Week 6 vs. Saints
headline: Jason Pinnock is out of concussion protocol and will play a part Sunday vs. the Saints; Theo Johnson's status awaits the 4:00 injury report.
summary: Harbaugh said Jason Pinnock has cleared the concussion protocol and will be part of the defensive plan Sunday, though he would not say how Pinnock and Jevon Holland will be deployed together. Asked about Theo Johnson, who was in the training room, Harbaugh deferred to the 4:00 injury report and would not address whether it is a long-term issue. He said the tackles who were limited earlier in the week looked fine in Friday's practice and expected a full-participation designation, but said he doesn't write the report. On ball security, Harbaugh said the fumbles came from getting the ball punched out rather than from weather or conditions, and that the team teaches a technique (the 'G-claw') and practices it in the Wednesday and Thursday sessions. He called the punch-out trend league-wide and said running backs and receivers must adjust, while the penalty for the 'peanut punch' is a point of emphasis for officials. Asked whether he would change running backs over fumbles, he said only 'We'll see.' He also used a Ray Lewis anecdote to explain that every player, including established starters, has to keep earning a job, and that injuries and performance open doors for competitors. The forecast of a clear, 57-degree day was welcome, but Harbaugh said the team must be careful with the ball regardless of weather.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Recaps Week 6, Gives Injury Updates
headline: Macdonald backs Sam Darnold as part of the fix, Anthony Bradford is likely back at right guard this week, and Elijah Arroyo's shoulder is still awaiting imaging results.
summary: Macdonald said the coaching staff has strong faith in Sam Darnold, who he believes is part of the solution despite turning the ball over too often. He framed the turnovers and the sacks as team-wide issues, not a quarterback-only problem, and said the offense will re-establish the Seahawks' identity under Brian Fleury, with a focus on the run game and on avoiding obvious passing downs. He credited the defensive staff for in-game adjustments that settled the unit after two long touchdown drives, while admitting he could have called some plays better. On Darnold's big plays outside the pocket, he said the team wants to encourage it but also needs to review how players work without the ball over the next 24 to 36 hours. Macdonald said Anthony Bradford has a good chance to return this week, which will factor into the right guard decision after the Haynes and Stephens rotation. He gave no update on Elijah Arroyo's shoulder beyond saying imaging and testing were underway. He also praised Rashid Shaheed's role and expects more intermediate-route targets to develop, and he pushed back on singling out any one player or unit for the offense's struggles.
